messages:
Maya: Quick ask — ACME PoC needs a short burst window on the hosted API next Tue 11:00-11:30 PT. They’ll run a client-side load test (~200 concurrent clients, ~12 rps each) to validate latency/cost. Org: org-acme-42. Can we provision a scoped key + temporary quota lift? :pray:
Ravi: Which model/endpoint are they hitting and what's the average tokens per request? That affects token/sec vs rps calculations.
Maya: They’ll be using text-generation -> endpoint /v1/generate, model: redwood-1.3-large. Avg ~480 tokens per response (including prompt). So target is ~200 * 12 * 480 ≈ 1.15M tokens/minute (peak). Looking for a safe request-rate window and a scoped key we can revoke.
Juniper: Capacity check — that token budget maps to ~19k tokens/sec. Us-west-2 hosted pool can absorb a 30m window if we reserve it; need to ensure no overlapping big customers. I can provision a scoped key and bump token quota for a 40-minute window (10m cushion). Need explicit times and fallback policy.
Noah: From security: scoped key only (no org master key), disable longer-term audit export for that key, redact PII in logs if possible, and add IP allowlist for their client runner. Can Maya confirm IP ranges?
Maya: Will get IPs by EOD. Can we also set a fallback to a lower-QPS model variant if the pool is saturated? Prefer automatic graceful degradation vs 429s.
Ravi: We can route fallback to redwood-1.3-small (same family, quantized) automatically via routing policy on the scoped key. That keeps latency predictable. Add a header so app logs which variant responded.
Tess: Steps I’ll take: 1) create a scoped API key with tag "acme-poc-loadtest" 2) set token_quota_per_minute to 1.3M 3) set valid_window to 2026-04-05T18:50:00Z/2026-04-05T19:30:00Z (30m window + 10m cushion) 4) add IP allowlist when provided. Sample create command:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"org_id":"org-acme-42","name":"acme-poc-loadtest","scopes":["gen:invoke"],"token_quota_per_minute":1300000,"valid_window":"2026-04-05T18:50:00Z/2026-04-05T19:30:00Z","routing_policy":{"fallback_model":"redwood-1.3-small"}}'
```
Juniper: I’ll reserve capacity and add a temp routing rule to prioritize this key on the us-west-2 pool during the window. Creating infra ticket now: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-4829
deploy-bot: INFRA ACTION: reserved 2.5k rps capacity on pool us-west-2 for tag "acme-poc-loadtest" — ticket INF-4829 — user: Juniper
Noah: Also add logging mask for prompt fields and set retention for this key to 7 days. Confirm once both are set.
Tess: Done — scoped key created (key id sk_acme_test_1945). Token quota = 1,300,000/min, fallback configured, logging mask applied, retention 7d. IP allowlist pending.
Maya: Confirmed, thanks team. I’ll share the scoped key and IPs with the ACME test runner. Please monitor latency/error-rate dashboards during the window and call out >1% 5xx or median latency >450ms. :thumbsup:
Juniper: Monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/poc/acme-1945. I’ll watch and can abort the window if there’s cross-customer impact.
Maya: Perfect — appreciate the quick turn.
Noah: Noted — security review complete for the temporary window.
Maya: Closing loop after the test, will post results and any regressions. Thanks everyone! :tada:
